lead: Lighter's acceptance of Robinhood stock tokens as perpetuals collateral extends competition over distribution into how traders can reuse assets, while Ostium's trading freeze shows how reopening prices can redistribute losses even when trader margin is held separately from the LP vault.

threads.title: Hyperliquid expands its equity perpetuals lineup
threads.update: This review found no major new equity perpetual or verified breakout in HIP-3 open interest after July 17. CXMT's listing was scheduled for July 27 and had yet to take place.
threads.watch: Convergence between CXMT's premarket and spot prices after July 27, changes in depth, and rules for index transitions or trading halts.

items.headline: Lighter accepts Robinhood stock tokens as collateral for perpetuals
body: **Event:** On July 20, Lighter began accepting Robinhood Stock Tokens as margin for perpetual positions, including tokens referencing NVDA, GOOG and AAPL. This is day 20 of the Robinhood distribution story, tracked since July 2.

**Mechanism:** The ERC-20 tokens are debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets Jersey. Lighter uses Chainlink price feeds to value them as margin. Unlike a deposit in USDG alone, this lets users retain equity exposure while backing perpetual positions with the same assets.

**Second-order effects:** Brokerage distribution now extends to collateral reuse. Equity volatility, issuer credit, price feeds and liquidation risk affect the same position. Users in the US and several other jurisdictions remain excluded.

context.label: Implementation
context.text: Stock tokens are eligible collateral. Haircuts, liquidation parameters, posted margin and utilization have not been disclosed.

items.headline: Ostium isolates trader margin, but a freeze and reopening price still allocate risk
body: **Event:** On July 20, Ostium confirmed a loss of 23.75 million USDC from the LP vault. Trader margin in a separate contract was not stolen. Open positions were frozen within 60 minutes of the attack. This was day seven of the oracle incident story, tracked since July 15.

**Mechanism:** The platform plans to provide at least 24 hours' notice before reopening and mark all frozen positions at the reopening price. Segregation protected trader principal, but users could not reduce positions, top up margin or hedge on the platform during the halt.

**Second-order effects:** The reopening price will allocate gains and losses accumulated during the halt. The incident report, LP compensation terms and reopening rules will shape confidence in the restart.

context.label: Scope
context.text: The LP vault lost 23.75 million USDC. Trader margin was not stolen. Compensation, the incident report and the reopening date were still pending.

items.headline: pump.fun makes BOOST buybacks and burns the default for newly graduated tokens
body: On July 21, pump.fun made BOOST the default migration mechanism for all eligible new tokens. After the bonding curve completes, the system executes time-weighted purchases within five minutes and burns the tokens it buys.

This redirects part of the liquidity previously locked in the pool into short-term buying and permanent burns. It can reduce a liquidity gap at migration, but support is concentrated in the opening five minutes. Later depth still depends on traders and market makers.

context.label: Measurement limits
context.text: The 17.6 SOL per pool and estimated 20% liquidity increase come from the platform. Post-migration depth and survival rates have yet to be verified.

items.headline: Risk parameters for stock tokens used as margin
body: **Benefit:** Users can retain exposure to their stocks without first converting to stablecoins and can use those holdings as collateral.
**Limitation:** Issuer credit, jurisdiction, price feeds and stock price gaps add risk to perpetual positions. Stablecoin liquidation parameters cannot simply be reused.
Assess collateral haircuts, position limits and liquidation capacity under stress separately before accepting equity tokens.

items.headline: Define the reopening price in the incident response rules
body: **Benefit:** Defining the freeze, notice and reopening price in advance shortens incident decisions and helps users understand how gains and losses will be settled.
**Limitation:** One reopening price cannot eliminate price gaps during a halt. A notice period cannot replace the ability to add margin, reduce a position or hedge.
Before trading resumes, operators should explain how open orders are handled, how positions are marked, when users will be notified and how markets will reopen in stages.
